description: Na₂ZnGe₂(HO₂)₄ crystallizes in the orthorhombic Pbcn space group. There are three inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded to six O atoms to form distorted NaO₆ octahedra that share  a cornercorner with one NaO₆ octahedra, corners with two equivalent ZnO₄ tetrahedra, corners with five GeO₄ tetrahedra, and edges with two NaO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 13°. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.41-2.56 Å. In the second Na site, Na is bonded to six O atoms to form distorted NaO₆ octahedra that share corners with two equivalent ZnO₄ tetrahedra, corners with six GeO₄ tetrahedra, and edges with two equivalent NaO₆ octahedra. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.42-2.63 Å. In the third Na site, Na is bonded to six O atoms to form distorted NaO₆ octahedra that share corners with two equivalent ZnO₄ tetrahedra, corners with six GeO₄ tetrahedra, and edges with two equivalent NaO₆ octahedra. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.45-2.59 Å. Zn is bonded to four O atoms to form ZnO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four NaO₆ octahedra and corners with four GeO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 66-67°. There are three shorter (1.98 Å) and one longer (1.99 Å) Zn-O bond length. There are two inequivalent Ge sites. In the first Ge site, Ge is bonded to four O atoms to form GeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with six NaO₆ octahedra and corners with two equivalent ZnO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 44-64°. There are two shorter (1.75 Å) and two longer (1.82 Å) Ge-O bond lengths. In the second Ge site, Ge is bonded to four O atoms to form GeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with five NaO₆ octahedra,  a cornercorner with one GeO₄ tetrahedra, and corners with two equivalent ZnO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 54-62°. There are a spread of Ge-O bond distances ranging from 1.75-1.82 Å. There are four inequivalent H sites. In the first H site, H is bonded in a single-bond geometry to two O atoms. There is one shorter (1.00 Å) and one longer (1.75 Å) H-O bond length. In the second H site, H is bonded in a single-bond geometry to two O atoms. There is one shorter (1.00 Å) and one longer (1.75 Å) H-O bond length. In the third H site, H is bonded in a single-bond geometry to two O atoms. There is one shorter (1.01 Å) and one longer (1.75 Å) H-O bond length. In the fourth H site, H is bonded in a single-bond geometry to two O atoms. There is one shorter (1.01 Å) and one longer (1.74 Å) H-O bond length. There are nine inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a distorted water-like geometry to three Na and two equivalent H atoms. In the second O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two Na, one Ge, and one H atom. In the third O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two Na, one Ge, and one H atom. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a 1-coordinate geometry to two Na, one Ge, and one H atom. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Zn, one Ge, and one H atom. In the sixth O site, O is bonded in a trigonal planar geometry to one Na and two equivalent Ge atoms. In the seventh O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Zn, one Ge, and one H atom. In the eighth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Zn, one Ge, and one H atom. In the ninth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Zn, one Ge, and one H atom.
